q1: SELECT NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S WHERE 0 = ( SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ORDERS AS O JOIN COMPANY AS C ON O.COM_ID = C.COM_ID WHERE O.SALES_ID = S.SALES_ID AND C.NAME = 'RED' )
q2: WITH CTE AS ( SELECT SALES_ID FROM ORDERS WHERE COM_ID=(SELECT COM_ID FROM COMPANY WHERE NAME='RED') ) SELECT S.NAME FROM SALESPERSON AS S LEFT JOIN CTE ON S.SALES_ID=CTE.SALES_ID WHERE CTE.SALES_ID IS NULL

explanation: Q1 finds salespersons who have zero orders associated with the company named 'RED'. Q2 finds salespersons who do not appear in the orders for the company named 'RED'. These queries are logically similar but not exactly equivalent due to subtle differences in handling LEFT JOIN and NULL conditions in Q2. A counterexample exists where Q1 and Q2 differ.
counterexample_dsp: A salesperson who has no orders at all (not even for 'RED') will be returned by Q2 but not by Q1 since Q1 checks for zero orders for 'RED'.
